findings.description: Run from inside a worktree, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns that worktree, not the main checkout. The script then prints "Skipped <name>: no worktree at .worktrees/<name>" while the worktree exists, and exits 0. An agent cleaning up its own worktree from its own cwd is a likely caller, and since kept or skipped names also exit 0, `worktree-remove.sh x && ...` cannot tell a no-op from a removal. Exit 0 on a kept dirty worktree is deliberate (the test at lines 164-165 asserts it); the wrong root is the real flaw, and the same pattern already exists in create and clean. One fix is to take ROOT from `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` and use its parent directory.

`--delete "$BRANCH"` uses the short name. If origin also has a tag with that name, git refuses the push ("dst refspec matches more than one"), so origin's branch is kept even though the lease and decision 30 aim at `refs/heads/` and same-named tags.

When the local tip is behind the merged PR's head, the branch is kept and the message wrongly says no merged PR shipped it. This happens when someone adds a commit on GitHub (a committed review suggestion or "Update branch") before a squash merge that auto-deletes the branch.

No test covers the merged-PR path when origin no longer holds the branch (forge auto-deleted the head branch, so REMOTE_TIP is empty); in both 'squashed' and 'moved' the local delete is also vouched for by origin holding the tip, so a regression making the local `git branch -D` depend on origin's copy would pass all 11 tests

The remove step sends stderr to /dev/null as well as stdout (the create step above only hides stdout), so if it fails in CI the log shows only 'failed to run' with no git error; the comment also says the branch is kept but nothing asserts it

The worktree.env comment 'remove and clean only touch this prefix' is wrong for remove: worktree-remove.sh removes the worktree whatever its branch and only limits branch deletion to the prefix (the 'never deletes a branch outside the configured prefix' test expects `.worktrees/spike` on `spike/other` to be removed)
Comment says the merged-PR question "goes unasked" without a working gh, but the script does ask and gets no answer. The ADR says "gh could not tell" while the script message says "gh could not say".
Header does not say that a failed fetch keeps every branch, which the code treats as a headline rule. The ADR and CHANGELOG both state it, and the code comment covers only the why.
Decision 29's "Not taken in here: the template's worktree-removal script" is now outdated, because decision 30 takes that script in. It could point forward to 30.

The branch-decision chain tracks gh state in the `CHECKED` and `MERGED_TIPS` pair, and `git branch -D "$BRANCH"` appears in two arms. Whether a branch is safe to delete is spread over three conditions, so the next rule has to be threaded through all of them.
The `cd "$ROOT"`, `worktree.env` sourcing and `PREFIX` default block is now copied verbatim into a third script, so a change to the config contract must be made in three places.

The new `remove()` helper re-implements `run()`'s spawnSync call and its `{status, stdout, stderr}` projection, differing only in the PATH stub. A change to the result shape would have to be made twice.
`--head` matches the head branch name only, with no owner filter, so a merged fork PR whose branch has the same name is also returned.

process_issues.description: The workflow's restore step should have copied the PR's versions of RESTORE_PATHS (AGENTS.md, .agents, templates) into .claude-pr/, but .claude-pr/ held only CLAUDE.md and .claude/. Reviewers read the PR's copies with `git show HEAD:<path>` instead, so coverage was not lost.

The diff is 9 files across several top-level areas, which passes the size gate. Only correctness was scaled to 2 instances: one on the script, one on tests and wiring. Security and maintainability ran as a single instance each, because the logic is all in one 74-line script.

The conventions reviewer did not open test/worktree.test.ts, so it did not check plan tests or snapshots for hard-coded script lists. The second correctness instance did confirm that the init test covers all three scripts' exec bits.
